_comment: The protection for the release TAGS, mirrored from the GitHub
Ruleset.
Apply it with:
python tools/apply_ci_ruleset.py --apply --mirror \
.github/rulesets/protect-tags.json
Why this exists
A release tag is the only thing that says which commit a
published artefact was built from.  Two operations destroy that
link, and neither is visible afterwards:
* deleting the tag, and
* moving the tag to a different commit (a force-update).
Neither is possible to undo in any way a consumer can observe:
the artefact is already published, the release page already
points at the old SHA, and the tag now says something else.
The `v1.2.0` case shows the shape of the risk.  The tag was cut
on `release/1.2`, that branch was `protected: false`, and the
repository's only ruleset covered `refs/heads/main` -- so
nothing stopped a force-push of the branch that carried the tag.
The tag itself survived (it is a separate ref), but the branch
it was cut from could have been rewritten underneath it, and the
release branch is what a `1.2.x` maintenance line is based on.
The rules here are deliberately minimal -- no `pull_request`, no
`required_status_checks`: a tag is not a branch, and a tag's
signature and form are already checked by
`tools/verify_tag_signature.py` (run by `release.yml`'s
preflight, in `--shape-only` mode).
name: protect-release-tags

_comment: The release tags only: `v1.0.0`, `v1.2.0`, ...  The
pattern covers every SemVer release tag, including the ones
cut later, with no further configuration.

rules._comment: A release tag cannot be deleted.

_comment: A release tag cannot be moved to another commit.  This is
the rule that keeps "the artefact was built from this
commit" true for as long as the tag exists.
